title: The Art of Deciding: How to Master Your Choices

mc.q: A manager chooses to ignore a rigorous decision-making process and selects TV monitor A over monitor B because he "trusts" company A more than company B. If the decision he made was rational, which one of the following is true?
o: Monitor A is really the better choice.
The manager should have included "trust" as a criterion.
Monitor B is really the better choice.
The manager must have made a mistake in calculating his weighted criteria.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. If trust drove the choice and the decision is to be rational, "trust" must be one of the explicit decision criteria (step 2 of the decision-making process).

mc.q: In allocating weights to the decision criteria, which one of the following is most helpful to remember?
o: All weights must be the same.
The total of the weights must equal 100.
The high score should be a 10, and no two criteria should be assigned the same weight.
Assign the most important criterion a score, and then assign weights against that standard.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Textbook: give the most important criterion a score (e.g. 10) and weight the others against that standard.

mc.q: Sondra has decided to purchase a new system. After obtaining permission, she has ordered the system from a reputable company. Which stage of the decision-making process is she carrying out in making the order?
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. The choice was already made; ordering = putting the decision into action (implementation).

mc.q: Maximizing value for an organization means making sure that ________.
o: the best interests of the organization are addressed
the decision made is as rational as possible
the decision is as simple as possible
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Rational decision making assumes decisions are made in the best interests of the organization.

mc.q: Which pair of terms is correctly matched up?
A key to what is commonly used to assess risk is for a decision maker to examine the ________ an investment.
o: promises made by a company for
ads posted by a company for

mc.q: Which one of the following is a primary characteristic of groupthink?
o: failure to reach consensus within a group
candidness and openness within a group

mc.q: Which one of the following is NOT a factor that can increase the probability of groupthink?
o: Influential group members dominate the discussion and the decision-making process.
Group leaders stress the importance of consensus above all other concerns.
The group has more than 40 group members.
Group leaders solicit ideas from all group members without passing judgment on their ideas.

mc.q: Which one of the following group techniques is relatively simple and is used exclusively to generate creative ideas in a group setting?
A manager can faithfully execute the decision-making process but still end up with nothing of value if ________.
o: he fails to identify the correct problem
he fails to assign number values to different criteria
he fails to correctly identify the steps of the process
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. If the wrong problem is identified, even a perfect process solves the wrong thing.

mc.q: A manager is considering purchasing new computers for her department. The manager spends time assessing the computers her department now has. Which stage of the decision-making process is she going through?
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Assessing the current situation (discrepancy between current and desired state) = identifying the problem.

mc.q: A manager is determining what kind of new computers she should purchase for her department. She has made a list of five different computer models for consideration. Which stage of the decision-making process is this?

After purchasing new computers for her department, a manager is now comparing the performance of the new computers to the computers they replaced. Which stage of the decision-making process is she carrying out?
For a high-tech bicycle buyer, decision criteria would be determined by ________.
What is a heuristic?
o: a complicated and systematic method of decision making
a purely intuitive method of decision making
a totally unreliable method of decision making
a shortcut or rule of thumb that is used for decision making

mc.q: Because they are not systematic or comprehensive, using heuristics in place of an eight-step decision-making process can lead to ________.
o: decisions that more directly solve problems

mc.q: A banker opts for short-term gain despite indications that his decision might not pay off in the long run. Which error or bias is the banker guilty of?
A scientist cites two studies that show a positive effect for her drug and ignores five other studies that show a negative effect. Which error or bias is she committing?
One legislator sees decreased tax revenue as the key problem in the budget. A second legislator sees increased spending as the problem. Each of these legislators has a(n) ________.
It is assumed that a rational decision maker ________.
o: would never make a wrong choice

mc.q: It is assumed that in most cases the decisions of all managers are limited by ________.
o: not being able to analyze all information for all alternatives
not being able to act rationally or in the best interests of their organization

mc.q: Which term best characterizes a decision that has bounded rationality?
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Bounded rationality leads to satisficing = accepting solutions that are "good enough".

mc.q: Which one of the following is the best definition for the word satisfice?
o: accepts a less than perfect solution
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Satisfice = accept a solution that is good enough, not perfect.

mc.q: Sticking to a decision despite evidence that it is a mistake is called ________.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Textbook definition of escalation of commitment.

mc.q: Which model of decision making takes advantage of unconscious reasoning?
mc.note: CORRECTED: B (nonrational) is circled on the sheet. The textbook defines intuitive decision making as making decisions on the basis of experience, feelings and accumulated judgment – "subconscious mental processing" is one of its explicit facets. Please double-check with your instructor.

mc.q: Structured problems are ________.
mc.note: On the sheet both A and C are circled. Structured problems are straightforward, familiar and easily defined → C.

mc.q: Unstructured problems are ________.
o: situations in which all options are known
situations in which all options are not known
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Unstructured problems are new/unusual, with ambiguous or incomplete information.

mc.q: Which one of the following is an example of a structured problem?
o: designing a new digital music player
deciding shipping options for a vacuum cleaner
drafting a quarterback for a pro football team
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Shipping options are a routine, recurring, well-defined decision; the others are new or unusual.

mc.q: Programmed decisions work well for solving ________.
mc.note: CORRECTED: B is circled on the sheet. Programmed decisions are repetitive decisions handled by a routine approach – they are used for STRUCTURED problems (see also question 5: structured problem ↔ programmed decision).

mc.q: Top managers in an organization tend to ________.
Which three conditions do decision makers face?
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Textbook: certainty, risk and uncertainty.

mc.q: ________ is a situation in which a decision maker has incomplete information about outcomes and does not have the ability to reasonably estimate outcomes that are not known.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Under risk, probabilities can be estimated; under uncertainty they cannot.

mc.q: One advantage of group decision making is that it usually provides ________ than individual decision making.
Group decisions generally feature ________ acceptance than decisions made by an individual.
Since all members of a group are rarely equal in status, most groups suffer from ________.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Textbook drawback of groups: minority domination – a few members dominate due to unequal status.

mc.q: Mid-level managers in a country with high power distance are ________ than managers from a low power distance country.
o: more likely to make risky decisions
less likely to make risky decisions
less likely to make safe, conservative decisions
more likely to disagree with their leaders' decisions
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. In high power distance cultures, important decisions are left to the top; mid-level managers defer and avoid risk.

mc.q: Mid-level managers in a country with low uncertainty avoidance are ________ than managers from a high uncertainty avoidance country.
o: more likely to make risky decisions
less likely to make risky decisions
less likely to make foolish decisions
more likely to avoid making decisions
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet. Low uncertainty avoidance = comfortable with ambiguity and risk.

mc.q: The use of ringisei in Japanese organizations reflects which one of the following values in Japanese culture?
mc.note: CORRECTED: A is circled on the sheet. Ringisei are consensus-forming group decisions – the textbook links them to the Japanese value of conformity and cooperation, i.e. consensus-seeking. Please double-check with your instructor.

mc.q: When dealing with international organizations, managers must be ________ in order to accommodate the managing styles of different cultures.
mc.note: Not marked on the sheet.

mc.q: Which one of the following tends to impede a person's creativity?

open: In a short essay, discuss why creativity is important to decision making. Describe a situation in which a creative solution is used to solve a problem.
In a short essay, describe how electronic meetings can help avoid groupthink and enhance creativity in group decision making.
In a short essay, discuss the differences among a procedure, a rule, and a policy. Include specific examples of each to support your answer.
In a short essay, list and discuss the first four steps in the decision-making process. Give an example of each step.
